title: When You're Tired of Doing Good and Nothing Seems to Change
paragraphs:
When You're Tired of Doing Good and Nothing Seems to Change
The Hidden Promise Inside Galatians 6:9 That Most Christians Never Fully Understand
Have you ever looked around and wondered if faithfulness is even making a difference?
You stayed when leaving would have been easier.
You carried burdens no one thanked you for carrying.
You kept choosing God while watching others choose shortcuts and somehow seem to prosper.
And somewhere deep inside, a dangerous question began whispering:
Not because you stopped loving Jesus.
The Apostle Paul understood that feeling more than most people realize.
That is why he wrote one of the most quoted, yet least understood verses in the entire New Testament:
"And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up." (Galatians 6:9)
Yet hidden inside those few words is a depth that often gets lost in modern reading.
Μὴ ἐγκακῶμεν δὲ ποιοῦντες τὸ καλόν, καιρῷ γὰρ ἰδίῳ θερίσομεν μὴ ἐκλυόμενοι.
Mē enkakōmen de poiountes to kalon, kairō gar idiō therisomen mē eklyomenoi.
A more literal rendering would be:
"Let us not lose heart while continually doing what is beautiful and good, because at the appointed season we shall harvest if we do not collapse inwardly."
Paul does not merely say, "Don't quit."
The Greek word ἐγκακῶμεν (enkakōmen) means far more than stopping.
It describes the moment when a person is still physically moving but spiritually exhausted.
But inwardly wondering if any of it matters.
Maybe everyone sees your strength while God alone sees your fatigue.
And that is exactly why this verse exists.
Because God has always known that weariness would become one of the greatest battles of genuine believers.
The enemy often cannot destroy a Christian through immediate temptation.
The tragedy is that many believers assume these thoughts mean they have weak faith.
The truth is often the opposite.
Weariness usually appears because you have been faithfully carrying a burden for a long time.
Nobody grows weary from doing nothing.
People grow weary from carrying weight.
And some of you have been carrying weight for years.
The Greek phrase is καιρῷ γὰρ ἰδίῳ (kairō gar idiō).
The word καιρός (kairos) refers to God's appointed moment.
A season established by God Himself.
This means your harvest is not controlled by your calendar.
And God's timing has never once failed.
The problem is that God often works underground before He works above ground.
Seeds disappear long before they appear.
The burial always looks like loss before it becomes growth.
Imagine digging up a seed every morning because you do not see immediate results.
You would destroy the very miracle you are waiting for.
Yet many believers do exactly that spiritually.
Walk away from God's process too soon.
They simply could not see it yet.
This truth becomes even more beautiful when viewed through the lens of the entire Gospel.
Because the greatest example of Galatians 6:9 is not us.
No one ever did more good than Christ.
Yet what did goodness seem to produce?
From a human perspective, Calvary looked like total failure.
The disciples thought everything was over.
But Heaven was not finished writing the story.
Because three days later, what looked like defeat became victory.
What looked like scandal became salvation.
What looked like death became resurrection.
This is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
This is why our theme is not merely a slogan.
The Hebrew Scriptures reveal this pattern repeatedly.
In Genesis 50:20 Joseph tells his brothers:
אַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטוֹבָה
"You intended evil against me, but God intended it for good."
The same God who rewrote Joseph's story is still rewriting stories today.
Perhaps yours is one of them.
Maybe you are reading this while sitting inside a chapter you never wanted.
A chapter filled with unanswered questions.
A chapter filled with tears nobody sees.
You may be judging your story from a chapter God has not finished yet.
And unfinished stories often look confusing.
The cross looked confusing on Friday.
That is why Galatians 6:9 is not simply encouragement.
It is an invitation to trust the Author.
To trust that every prayer matters.
Nothing offered to Christ is ever wasted.
Not one whispered prayer in the dark.
And He remembers all of it.
Maybe you are tempted to stop.
Then hear the voice of Scripture again:
"Let us not lose heart while doing good."
Not because the struggle is small.
And faithful people eventually discover what weary people cannot yet see.
But because the God who planted the promise never forgets where He planted the seed.
If this message reached you exactly when you needed it, do not keep it to yourself.
Let them know their story is not over.
What season are you currently walking through?
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
One day you will discover that the season that almost made you quit became the testimony that proved God never left.
